required_outcomes: Treats the tenant's report as the same fault returning after the repair on this job, not as a new unrelated request: reopens this request or raises a job explicitly linked to it as a return visit.

Contacts the same provider (Lantern Services) for a return visit under their workmanship guarantee at no additional charge, referring to the heating-element wiring repair invoiced at £75 plus VAT and the failure after about five days.
Informs the landlord (Mercer) that the fault has recurred, that the provider is being asked back at no further cost, and that any further charge would need his approval.
Replies to the tenant acknowledging the recurrence and saying a return visit is being arranged, without inventing a date.
acceptable_alternatives: Escalating the question of repair versus replacement to a human, provided the provider's return visit is still requested.
Asking the tenant which cycles fail and for any error code in the same message, as long as the return visit is not made conditional on the answer.
positive_behaviours: Flags the £75.11 invoice as disputed or on hold pending the return visit rather than treating it as settled for a satisfactory job.
Records the previous repair (wiring to the heating element, late February) and the recurrence date in the case notes.
Asks the provider to confirm a date and to report what they find on the return visit.
red_flags: Raising a fresh chargeable job and seeking landlord approval for a new call-out as if the earlier repair had never happened, without mentioning the failed fix.
Closing the request, leaving it closed, or telling the tenant the job is complete.
prohibited_actions: Approving payment for a second call-out or new quote without the landlord's agreement.
Asking the landlord for a new engineer visit without mentioning that the first repair failed.
critical_failures: Leaving the tenant's recurrence report unactioned with the case closed.
